**Observations from the image:**

- **Affected part**: Banana leaf (large, elongated monocot leaf)
- **Spot morphology**: Multiple discrete oval-to-round lesions scattered across the leaf blade
- **Spot color**: Grayish-tan/pale brown centers with darker brown borders
- **Halo**: Yellowish halos visible around several spots, particularly along the leaf margin
- **Distribution**: Spots of varying sizes scattered irregularly; some coalescing near the margins
- **Leaf margin**: Yellowing and necrosis along the edges

**Differential reasoning:**

| Class | Match? |
|---|---|
| **Bunchy_Top** | No — no bunching/rosetting; no dark vein streaks |
| **Cigar_End_Rot** | No — this affects fruit tips, not leaf blades |
| **Panama_Disease** | No — wilt/yellowing pattern from pseudostem, not discrete leaf spots |
| **Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka** | Partial — Sigatoka lesions typically start as streaks/elongated marks, not discrete round spots |
| **Anthracnose** | Partial — primarily a fruit/post-harvest disease; lesions usually darker and more sunken |
| **Cordana_Leaf_Spot** | **Yes** — caused by *Cordana musae*; classic presentation: oval/round spots with pale gray-tan centers, dark brown margins, and diffuse yellow halos, scattered across the leaf blade |

The discrete oval lesions with light gray centers, dark brown borders, and yellow halos are the hallmark presentation of **Cordana Leaf Spot**, distinguishing it from Sigatoka (streak-like) and Anthracnose (darker, more sunken on fruit).
